# Pi NFT Fee Reconciliation — llms.txt
# A read-only, zero-dependency reconciler between a declared NFT-marketplace fee
# schedule (basis points) and the fees actually observed in on-chain events.

> A published fee schedule is a claim, not a measurement. The only way to know
> whether a stated fee was actually charged is to compare it against what the
> chain recorded. This tool does that comparison deterministically.

## What it is
- read-only, zero-dependency, Node (ESM), Node >= 18
- fee-check.mjs: the CLI (--config --events --tolerance)
- test.mjs: 12 offline checks (node --test)
- never writes; no database; no API keys

## Why it exists
Marketplaces publish a fee schedule, but a published number is a claim, not a
measurement. This tool recomputes the EXPECTED fee from the declared rate and the
observed amount, and reports any mismatch, so a reviewer can see the discrepancy
directly instead of trusting a dashboard.

## Input formats
fees.json — declared schedule in basis points (1 bps = 0.01 %):
  { "listBps": 0, "buyBps": 250, "acceptBps": 0, "currency": "PI" }
events.json — array (or { "events": [...] }) of observed events:
  [ { "type": "buy", "amount": "12.5", "fee": "0.3125", "tx": "..." } ]

## Output shape
Per event: [n] type amount= expected= observed= OK|MISMATCH. Then a # Summary:
events_checked, matched, mismatches.
Exit codes: 0 all matched; 2 one or more mismatches; 1 error.

## Tolerance
Fees are computed in floating point, so --tolerance (same unit as the amounts,
default 0) absorbs rounding at the last displayed digit. Set 0 for exact.

## Usage
- node fee-check.mjs --config fees.json --events events.json
- node fee-check.mjs --config fees.json --events events.json --tolerance 1
- node --test test.mjs

## Not claimed
- that the declared rate is CORRECT (it only checks whether the observed fee
  matches the declared rate)
- that no fee was taken outside the checked events (it reconciles only the events
  supplied)
- that the events are authentic (the caller supplies them; their provenance is a
  separate question)
- that the venue owns the fee-receiving address (on-chain data never proves venue
  ownership)
- that Pi Network has adopted, reviewed or endorsed this
